As a child, she had been told she couldn’t have children, and after years of trying during marriage, she eventually accepted that reality. But in 2023, after walking through divorce, addiction recovery, and one of the hardest seasons of her life, she stared down at a positive pregnancy test in complete shock. “I didn’t tell anyone,” Natally shared. “I felt so alone at that time.” Fear quickly took over. The father of the baby did not want to be involved, and Natally became overwhelmed by the thought of raising a child completely on her own. Though she had been raised in church, she admitted that for the first time in her life, abortion crossed her mind. “If I don’t go through with this,” she thought, “all the criticism will come back. If I do, no one will ever know.” Natally walked into the Clinic carrying fear, shame, uncertainty, and the weight of everything she had been through. But instead of judgment, she found compassion. Someone listened to her, held her hand, and reminded her that her story was not over. Then came the ultrasound. Natally admitted she was terrified. “I refused, at first, to even look at it (the screen),” she said. “It was the hardest thing.” But when she finally looked up, she saw something she says she will never forget. “The sac she was in was heart-shaped,” Natallyshared. “I felt like it was God giving me peace.” That moment changed everything. Today, Natally’s daughter is thriving after surviving an extremely premature birth at just 24 weeks. Natally calls her daughter “my miracle” and “my medicine.” Friend, stories like Natally’s are why PreBorn! exists. It's thanks to these women — like my mom, who served in the U.S. Navy, raised four kids as a military wife, and devoted 25 years to Indian education at the Bureau of Indian Affairs — that I summoned the courage to run for office.

**And it led me to become one of the first Native American women elected to Congress and, later on, the first Native American Cabinet secretary in U.S. history.**

https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
Trump promised lower costs, renewed manufacturing, and no more endless wars.
Instead, Americans got higher prices, economic chaos, and another disastrous war in the Middle East.
* Inflation is up.
* Gas averages $4.53 per gallon.
* Energy prices have surged 18%.
Farmers are hurting. Manufacturers are struggling. Working families are falling further behind.
The reality is that Trump has no vision to improve Americans’ lives. It’s up to us to address these challenges. That starts with rebuilding American industry, empowering workers, and restoring faith in government by actually delivering results. I call this a new economic patriotism.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. While we honor our fallen heroes, the Democrats' handpicked candidate is mocking them.

Friend,

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hey Peter — it’s Gina.
**I’d love to give you a quick call and chat, just the two of us! 📞**
In the last seven months since we launched this campaign, we’ve built real momentum and people-power to take on Greg Abbott and the wealthy few who’ve run Texas for too long — and it’s all because of your support. I’m so thankful to have you on this journey with me.
But this fight is just getting started, and I want to check in so I can learn what matters most to you and discuss how we can win this race together. I also want to personally say thank you and share a small token of my appreciation.
**[Peter, if you’re able to chip in $5 or anything else today, you could be one of the supporters I’ll personally call. I’d love the chance to connect with you!](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260523_1_calls.ArmeEU&refcode=em20260523-1173&amount=5&t=1&akid=1173%2E299639%2EMh45g9)**

When I launched this campaign, I said something my grandmother taught me: _“No te dejes.”_ **Don’t back down. Don’t let them take what’s ours.**
You’ve already shown you won’t, and that you believe Texas’ future is worth fighting for. Now I want to hear directly from you. Whether you’re worried about your kid’s school, tired of Abbott putting his billionaire donors first, or just want to share what’s giving you hope, I’ll be listening. It’s what keeps this movement going, and if you can donate now, you might just get a call from me soon to say thanks!](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260523_1_calls.ArmeEU&refcode=em20260523-1173&amount=5&t=3&akid=1173%2E299639%2EMh45g9)**

Thank you for your support. I hope to talk with you soon!
Gina

Not so long ago, Iowa ranked number one in public education. Iowa was a national destination for young families seeking great public schools. Our public schools were a source of pride.

Right now, two of the oldest justices on the court — Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas — could retire at any moment. And when they do, Donald Trump names their replacements. That could mean much younger and much more extreme MAGA Republicans who will be on that bench for decades. We've already seen what happens when Trump picks justices. Roe v. Wade — gone. Voting rights — gutted. Worker rights — threatened. Trump's justices have sided, over and over again, with extremists and giant corporations over working people. Now, imagine the damage they could do if there were two more of them? **What do we do about it? We take back the Senate. If Democrats have the Senate majority, we can block his extremist nominees. If Republicans hold the Senate, Trump gets a rubber stamp for any nominee he wants, no questions asked.** These midterms are critical. Not just for us, but for the kids who will inherit this country. For the grandkids who will grow up under the decisions this court makes. For the generations who come after that. [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek,

We have a Republican Congress of weak sycophants who have abdicated their
constitutional responsibilities and abandoned all of us to serve the will
of Donald Trump.

The last thing we can afford is to give Trump another rubber stamp here in
Pennsylvania — but that’s exactly what we’re up against in this race.

My opponent is running on her complete and total allegiance to Donald
Trump — because she’s more focused on serving him than fighting for you.

She proudly wears her MAGA hat, while I wear the Pennsylvania jersey.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/763?t=1001&akid=48%2E245147%2EZmMVKD ]Derek,
Pennsylvanians deserve a Governor who shares

always be that kind of Governor — which is exactly why Donald Trump and

| A personal note from Steve | Before June 2nd
---|---
Dear Friend, I wrote this because I do not want this moment to pass quietly. You get a lot of campaign emails. I know that. Most of them are overly urgent and instantly forgettable.
| | ★ |
---|---|---
Deadlines. Buttons. Exclamation points. The usual performance. **This is not that.** I wrote you a real note because **June 2nd is almost here** , and after that, this race moves on with us or without us.
|
---
Please read what I wrote | [Read My Message](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| There is no automatic Republican nominee in California. There is no second chance if we fall short. There is no clever explanation that will make up for failing to do everything possible while there was still time.
---
**That is the brutal, unavoidable fact.** And frankly, I do not want this to be the last serious message I send to Americans across the country about this campaign because Democrats managed to stop us before November. **That would be a bitter, ridiculous ending to a fight we can absolutely win.**
| Before the window closes Help me keep this campaign moving. | [Stand With Me](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
So before you scroll past another campaign email, I want you to read the note I wrote. It explains exactly where this race stands, why Democrats want us buried before June 2nd, and why I believe they are terrified of facing us one-on-one in November. They should be.
|
---
_Thank you,_
_Steve Hilton_

Trump isn’t even pretending to hide the corruption anymore. If you commit

Not health care. Not housing. Not lowering costs for working families.
Just a billion-dollar payoff scheme for loyalists who attacked the Capitol
on his behalf.

This is what authoritarian corruption looks like: weaponized government,
public money flowing to extremists, and a president treating the Treasury
like his personal loyalty rewards program.

And if Trump can get away with this, imagine what comes next.

Demand Justice is fighting back against Trump, his MAGA cronies, and the

Thankfully, I’m not alone. Huge majorities of Americans believe the Supreme Court is ruling against the Constitution and acting unethically. The people are tired of a system that takes our power away and gives it to the wealthy and well-connected.

clean_body: We rallied at the Capitol on Wednesday. Here’s how it went >> | | Peter, On Wednesday, we showed up at the Capitol to demand that our leaders stop treating the Supreme Court’s attacks on voting rights like business as usual. They had no choice but to hear us. Over 100 people showed up with signs, microphones, and chants. Over 400,000 more joined online. Our lineup of speakers included allies from Planned Parenthood, End Citizens United, and the National Education Association. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse and Representative Analilia Mejia spoke out about Supreme Court corruption. As a Louisianan whose community is directly impacted by the Supreme Court’s decision in Louisiana v. Callais, I was honored to take the stage. This fight isn’t just a headline for me—it’s personal. I’d like to encourage you to take a few minutes to watch and share my remarks. The right-wing media echo chamber doesn’t want people to know that we can fight back against the corrupt Supreme Court and the wannabe dictator in the White House. That’s why every share helps us break through and build the grassroots movement for court reform. | The Supreme Court’s decision didn’t just gut the Voting Rights Act. It serves to eliminate Black voting power in the South, and blessed racial gerrymandering across the country. The ruling stole the votes of the community I grew up in, and I refuse to be silent in the face of these attacks on our rights and our democracy. Thankfully, I’m not alone. Huge majorities of Americans believe the Supreme Court is ruling against the Constitution and acting unethically. The people are tired of a system that takes our power away and gives it to the wealthy and well-connected. Like I said in my remarks, our judicial institution was created to ensure equal justice amongst all people, not to defend and aid one single person. When people hear about what’s going on at the Supreme Court, they see the corruption as clear as day. And the more we break through in the news and on social media, the more people we’ll mobilize to take action and fight back. Thank you for amplifying our fight far and wide, Ken’Travius Coleman United for Democracy Paid for by United for Democracy. | | Sent via . Comedian and former Trump supporter Tim Dillon went on Piers Morgan this week and said something that perfectly explains the moment the Republican Party is living through right now:
_**Donald Trump 's betrayal of his own voters is "the biggest betrayal of a political movement I've ever seen in my life."**_
And honestly, I think a lot of people inside MAGA quietly know that's true.
Because what's happening right now is bigger than Republicans purging Thomas Massie or Trump endorsing Ken Paxton over John Cornyn or another ugly primary fight inside the party. What we're watching is the slow unraveling of the anti-establishment coalition that made Trump possible in the first place.
* * *
**Today 's rant is sponsored by Ground News.**
I've been paying more attention to how differently the same story gets covered depending on where you read it--especially lately, when everything feels optimized for speed and outrage instead of context.
Take this one--hundreds of outlets picked up reports questioning the true cost of Trump's "Golden Dome."
**RocketNews** says _Trump 's "Golden Dome" could cost trillions and still fall short against major missile attacks_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/db1e23e9-f58c-4b9e-9eac-7baaf3b7311b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Welt** states _ "Experts lack enough detail" _to estimate the long-term price of Trump's missile shield plan
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/db1e23e9-f58c-4b9e-9eac-7baaf3b7311b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Same story--completely different narratives.

That's why I use Ground News. It pulls together 50,000+ sources so you can compare coverage side by side, see political bias, who owns the sources you're reading, how reliable they are and understand how framing changes the story.

You can literally watch how the left vs right headline the same event--and what each side emphasizes (or leaves out).

They also highlight stories you might be missing entirely in their Blindspot Feed which shows you stories that are disproportionately reported by either side of the political spectrum.

I've been a paying user since before they ever sponsored Endless Urgency. I use it because it makes it a lot harder to be misled. They're completely subscriber funded so there are no corporate interests pushing a narrative on what you see.

See the full picture, instead of just one angle with Ground News. [Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/2262cbef-6657-4846-ae97-e1922156457a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Trump built his entire movement around the idea that he was going to fight the political establishment instead of becoming part of it. He promised people he would end forever wars, expose corruption, release the Epstein files, lower costs for working Americans, and break a system that millions of voters believed had stopped working for them.
Instead, a lot of those voters now look around and see another Middle East conflict spiraling out of control, an economy that feels brutal for ordinary people, connected insiders getting richer, and Republicans demanding absolute loyalty to Trump no matter what happens.
That's where the frustration inside MAGA is coming from.
And I think Democrats misunderstand this when they reduce every Trump voter to being stupid or evil or brainwashed. A lot of these people were genuinely angry about corruption, economic inequality, endless war, and institutions that felt completely disconnected from normal life in America. Trump tapped into that frustration better than any politician in decades.
The problem is that instead of dismantling that system, he increasingly became a version of it.
That's why figures like Tim Dillon, Tucker Carlson, Candace Owens, and even parts of the online MAGA ecosystem are starting to fracture away from Trump over issues like Iran, the Epstein files, and government corruption. These are people whose audiences bought into the idea that Trump was different, and now they're struggling to explain why his presidency increasingly looks like the same Republican politics they thought they were rejecting.
And honestly, the Massie situation tells you everything you need to know about what the Republican Party has become.
Massie is not some liberal hero. He's a conservative libertarian from Kentucky who voted with Republicans the overwhelming majority of the time. But the moment he publicly challenged Trump over Iran, spending, and the Epstein issue, he became politically disposable.
That's because the modern Republican Party is no longer really organized around policy or ideology. It's organized around personal loyalty to Donald Trump.
And while MAGA influencers celebrate Trump consolidating control over the party, I think they're missing the bigger picture entirely. Yes, Trump dominates Republican primaries. But at the same time, independent voters are drifting away from him, younger voters are exhausted by the chaos, and even parts of his own coalition are becoming disillusioned with what his movement has turned into.
That matters politically.
Because Americans are deeply frustrated right now, and not just with Republicans. People feel like the economy isn't working for them. They feel like institutions are dishonest. They feel like politicians spend more time performing outrage online than improving anyone's life. And they're tired of watching powerful people profit while ordinary families struggle to afford housing, groceries, healthcare, and basic stability.
That frustration created Trump in the first place.
* * *
_**Mid-rant note:**_**this section is sponsored by Ground News.**
I've started paying more attention to how the same story can feel completely different depending on who's reporting it. Ground News makes that easy to see by showing coverage from across the political spectrum and pointing out what certain outlets leave out.
My team and I use it because it helps cut through the noise.
**[If you want a clearer view of what's actually going on, check out Ground News ->](https://substack.com/redirect/db1e23e9-f58c-4b9e-9eac-7baaf3b7311b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
_Give it a try!_
[ Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/2262cbef-6657-4846-ae97-e1922156457a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
And if Democrats don't understand the underlying anger driving this moment, the country is eventually going to produce somebody even more dangerous -- somebody smarter, more disciplined, and more effective than Trump ever was.
That's why I take people like Tucker Carlson seriously even though I disagree with most of what they believe. Democrats made the mistake of dismissing Trump as a joke because he looked ridiculous and sounded ridiculous. Meanwhile, he was building a direct emotional connection with millions of Americans who felt abandoned by both parties.
The warning signs are there again now.
People are desperate for authenticity. They want leaders who sound like they actually understand what life feels like outside elite political circles. They want somebody willing to acknowledge that the system is broken instead of constantly pretending everything is fine while costs explode and trust in institutions collapses.
And whichever political movement figures out how to channel that frustration into something real is going to shape the next era of American politics.
Because Trump was never the root problem. He was the product of a country where millions of people lost faith that the system was working for them anymore.
And until somebody actually fixes that, this cycle is just going to keep producing angrier voters, more distrust, more extremism, and politicians who are better and better at weaponizing despair against a country that already feels like it's falling apart.
Whichever movement restores that without exploiting people's anger is going to define the future of this country.

This spring, [Mt. Joy](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/67685?t=3&akid=240864%2E444211%2EuE-Jqj) was looking for a voter registration partner to join their Texas tour dates. We jumped on the opportunity, and our teams in Dallas and Austin got to work.
On April 25th, our DFW team — led by Jay, Darrel, and Diandra — set up under our assigned canopy at the Longhorn Backyard Amphitheater next to the merch table.
We canvassed the crowd all evening, checking voter registration statuses, updating records for folks who'd moved, and talking about what's at stake this November.
By the end of the night, we'd helped check over 200 voter statuses — and found a few people who thought they were registered but weren't on the rolls. Good thing they checked.
The band even donated a signed vinyl for us to raffle off to folks who stopped by to check their registration status.
The very next night, April 26th, our Austin team — led by Wes — brought that same energy to the Moody Center.
We were joined by local volunteers and one of our Texas State interns, Gallant, who drove in from San Marcos just to help out. We worked the main lobby, concession lines, and venue entrances — meeting people wherever they were.
In just one hour, we added 81 new contacts to our contact list and recruited 2 new volunteers.
This is what organizing looks like. Showing up where people already are, in moments they're already enjoying.
We're planning to bring this model to more concerts this summer across Texas. More venues. More crowds. We’ll register people to vote, check their status, and then stay personally connected with them through Election Day and beyond to make sure they cast a ballot.
[**But organizing at huge events like these take resources — for staff time, materials, and the volunteer coordination that makes it all run smoothly. If you believe in this kind of grassroots, meet-people-where-they-are organizing, please consider chipping in $3 today.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260523.eahp5b&refcode=ema20260523-240864&t=4&akid=240864%2E444211%2EuE-Jqj)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260523.eahp5b&refcode=ema20260523-240864&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=23&akid=240864%2E444211%2EuE-Jqj)**
Thank you for making this work possible.
Aimee Prudhomme

body:
The GOP and Big Oil are trying to stop New York from fighting climate change. |
---
Peter — Climate change is an existential and urgent threat to the future of our planet. The dramatic increase in natural disasters is no accident. But instead of acknowledging this reality, Republicans in Congress are attempting to pass legislation to block New York’s _Climate Change Superfund Act._ New York’s “Polluters Pay” law holds the oil and gas industry accountable for the pollution they cause. If Republicans succeed, this would let Big Oil off the hook, passing the $3 billion cleanup price tag onto taxpayers. The law is also critical to the state’s ability to prepare for the effects of climate change. The funds paid by polluters won’t just help clean up their messes — they will also fund infrastructure repairs and resilience measures to help prepare for future disasters. **Republicans won’t do anything to make your life more affordable, but they’ll always bend over backwards to send taxpayer’s hard-earned money to pump up Big Oil.** I will forcefully oppose any attempts to preempt the _Climate Change Superfund Act_ , because polluters, not New Yorkers, should foot the bill for the environmental harm they cause. **My message is simple: clean up your own damn mess.** **[Now, I’m calling on you to join me. A humbling message...
| Peter,
---
I’m truly humbled and honored.
---
Direct from the White House, my friend President Trump said:
---
**“JIM JORDAN IS A VERY GOOD FRIEND, FIGHTER, AND WINNER... HE WILL _NEVER_ LET YOU DOWN”**

[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=c27984e9034342ba813f0148f76b47c7&_e=yg-C90d9V7s1-9EDLS8hIeELTY8VkFO6G1nz2RKbv7oSR-H3lIRYcxJwe-LBJtBmxkQzsRjam_q4IQjLz0SHQjWScj_PciCKD_i1WIeHmhUaAZ8WR0Z8LDQFtQcWk4t3QkmZbXsjL5a9tKY29naSbvLW2HdhqlTrRmbJamKZETNRyvqvIWo-w04oVEHIP8o6mmJp_bPcRrZCDlw92OdxLVMi0bZaIenTlwiW_obT4fssD-lLPc564liEae4mNoBCx_rj7Po8dFiByLUr8VTjNsVKbzNBP6YyMuxvCoIpdQQ7weBDMCUUWi77sIcK9xZbXQCfABWgtHJ--C8YZS8DNNncPf0y1lAb1-s7F-vbfr4RhoWKFZQ6blzW2B0fzf5WyNLq87WziapriEw0ak8Z2B1V6Qk7T9CIhRLiC_e1R1zfOeYwm5Hj6VjLdEPQLB8wRtWPOie52Ja20zZD129Dk4dNyCLtuA13jrtPjGEqoTpzyw-yKfaSxznNj842JbDiXP10EtjG4G-UKlaRXc1Qto0kSispKXB1uxSZ7Winj1DcxT15ui8fHkLpuz6SoexQ7i43K1zPTnkhG8FSamNpRA%3D%3D)

Coming from the President, those are powerful words.

President Trump knows _better than anyone_ the fight I’m waging to drain the swamp and put power back where it belongs – with _YOU_ , the American people.
---
Look, I know talk is cheap in politics. Anyone can make a promise. Anyone can say they’ll fight.
---
**But I’ve got the receipts to back it up**. I’ve been sued. I’ve been spied on. My phone records were seized. And the Left only attacks me, because I fight for YOU.
---
**I’m working with the President – _behind the scenes and all hours of the day_ – to deliver on the agenda you voted for.**
---
And directly from the Oval Office, President Trump laid out the agenda **WE** are fighting for:
---
_**✅Grow our economy
✅Cut taxes
✅Slash burdensome regulations
✅Promote Made-In-The-USA products
✅Champion American energy dominance
✅Keep our border secure
✅Stop migrant crime
✅Defend your constitutional rights
✅Stopping the Radical Left ** _
---
And in just a few months, that same agenda will be voted on AGAIN in the midterm elections.
---
There’s been a lot of doom and gloom about our odds of holding the House. But truth be told, Democrats now ONLY have a **2-POINT** advantage over us.
---
And that’s not because voters suddenly approve of Radical Left ideas._It’s simply because our side isn’t showing up to vote._
---
**If 2% more Republicans show up, we can EASILY erase the Democrats’ 2-point lead. This is a problem we can absolutely fix.**
---
_So, we are going zip code by zip code in our voter file to determine where we need more participation._
---
Peter, we’ve crunched the numbers and with our razor-thin majority now within the margin of error, YOUR voter profile in your zip code is the difference maker.
---
_That’s why I’m reaching out today to simply ask that you VERIFY your GOP voter profile to give me and President Trump the most accurate polling possible to ERASE the Democrats’ 2% LEAD over us._
---

**"**_**We just need to mess around**_**" -Bill Gates [2021 annual letter](https://substack.com/redirect/6c60a7e9-5bb8-4098-b5ab-4b8a09f5c64d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on pandemic planning in reference to the ongoing research of mRNA technology**
On January 7, 2026, the[Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations](https://substack.com/redirect/cd372730-1815-461c-9799-53114b047d6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)(CEPI)--a global vaccine-development coalition launched at Davos in 2017 with significant backing from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation--announced up to $26.7 million in new funding. The money was awarded to a consortium led by the University of Oxford's Vaccine Group and Pandemic Sciences Institute, working alongside Leipzig University's Institute for Drug Discovery and Moderna. The objective was to design and test multivalent vaccine candidates against the filovirus family, including Ebola virus, Sudan virus,[Bundibugyo virus](https://substack.com/redirect/9ba4c10d-5242-4982-9a43-4db4349e1d46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Marburg virus, and even unknown future filoviruses.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=198982392&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk4OTgyMzkyLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk1NTYxMDEsImV4cCI6MTc4MjE0ODEwMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.M-Oo6_0gxWj_G14R9yvVZKoZ9nD6R8GIt8cBZ9EDwGg)
Exactly four months later, between May 15 and May 17, 2026, health authorities were confronted with something epidemiologists had not seen in over a decade: a major, cross-border outbreak of Ebola disease caused specifically by the Bundibugyo virus in the[Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://substack.com/redirect/3d81e459-447b-4866-8a2e-32ec0f63b753?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)(DRC) and Uganda. By May 17, the World Health Organization (WHO) had declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). As of late May, health officials were tracking roughly 500 suspected cases and more than 130 deaths, including an infected American healthcare worker evacuated from the region.

**What Is Bundibugyo Virus?**
Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) is one of four known Ebola virus species that cause disease in humans. It belongs to the Filoviridae family, placing it in the same biological category as the better-known Zaire ebolavirus (the strain behind the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic and the ERVEBO vaccine) and the even deadlier Marburg virus.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.vTHr__uXSH3cakpuLbM6_VooBOuN_ApxvoN65U16FYA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=198982392)

The pathogen was first discovered in 2007 during an outbreak in the Bundibugyo district of western Uganda. Genetic analysis later confirmed it was distinct from other Ebola strains. It caused a second confirmed outbreak in 2012 in Isiro, Province Orientale, DRC, resulting in 38 confirmed cases and 13 deaths. Since then, it had remained largely dormant in the global public health consciousness--until May 2026.

Bundibugyo virus disease presents with nonspecific early symptoms--sudden fever, intense headache, fatigue, muscle pain, and sore throat--that mimic severe malaria or influenza. This overlap makes initial clinical diagnosis difficult. The illness can progress to gastrointestinal symptoms, organ dysfunction, and hemorrhagic manifestations. Historical case fatality rates range from approximately 30% to 50%, comparable to or slightly lower than Zaire ebolavirus, but still devastating.

Ebola is primarily transmitted**through direct, unprotected contact with the bodily fluids of an infected, symptomatic person or deceased body**. Common fluids that carry the virus include blood, saliva, sweat, vomit, feces, urine, breast milk, and semen.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de5c8387-285f-461f-bdc6-c07b2d8e7a29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Critically, no licensed vaccines or specific treatments currently exist for Bundibugyo virus disease. The two approved Ebola vaccines--such as Merck's ERVEBO--protect only against Zaire ebolavirus, not Bundibugyo. Diagnostic complexity adds another layer of risk: standard Ebola tests can miss Bundibugyo, meaning outbreaks can circulate undetected for weeks before laboratory confirmation.

**What Did the $26.7 Million Buy?**
Contrary to some social media framings, CEPI's January 2026 grant did not purchase a single, strain-specific "Bundibugyo mRNA shot." Rather, it funded an ambitious, broadly protective ("multivalent") vaccine program targeting multiple filoviruses simultaneously.

Here is what the money specifically underwrote, according to CEPI, Oxford, and CIDRAP:
* **A dual-platform approach** : The Oxford team is leveraging its ChAdOx viral vector technology--the same platform used in its COVID-19 and other investigational vaccines--while Moderna contributes its mRNA platform. Both platforms will be used to test and compare multivalent candidates.
* **AI-driven antigen design** : Researchers at Leipzig University's Institute for Drug Discovery are using artificial intelligence to design vaccine components targeting shared, "conserved" features across the filovirus family.
* **Bundibugyo as a named target** : CEPI's official announcement explicitly lists Bundibugyo virus among the program's priority targets, alongside Ebola virus (Zaire), Sudan virus, and Marburg virus. The goal is not merely to stockpile single-strain vaccines but to create an "all-in-one" filovirus vaccine that could protect against known strains and potentially future, as-yet-unidentified family members.
* **Preclinical development** : As of the January 2026 announcement, the Oxford-Leipzig-Moderna consortium was in the **preclinical** phase. The $26.7 million--co-funded by CEPI and the European Union's Horizon Europe program--was earmarked for early-stage design, laboratory testing, and candidate screening, not for immediate human trials or stockpiled doses.
CEPI's active portfolio documents from early 2026 confirm this entry as a "Broadly protective Filovirus vaccine" at the preclinical stage, combining viral vector and mRNA approaches.

**The Four-Month Gap**
The chronology is verifiable and striking:

* **January 7, 2026** : CEPI announces the $26.7 million Oxford-Leipzig-Moderna award.
* **May 15, 2026** : DRC's Ministry of Health declares an Ebola outbreak in Ituri Province; genomic sequencing at the National Institute for Biomedical Research in Kinshasa confirms the **Bundibugyo strain**. Uganda confirms cross-border cases the same day.
* **May 17, 2026** : WHO convenes and declares the outbreak a PHEIC.
This is roughly four months between the funding announcement and the outbreak declaration.

Global health officials, including CEPI itself, have responded to the outbreak by activating emergency scientific and funding coordination teams. Scientific American reported on May 20, 2026, that CEPI was "exploring ways to rapidly advance vaccine candidates" tied to the current crisis. CEPI has long advocated a "prototype pathogen" or "viral family" approach--preparing for entire families of viruses rather than betting on one strain at a time. In this framework, the January funding fits CEPI's longstanding mission, which since 2017 has prioritized Ebola, Lassa, MERS, Nipah, and other emerging threats.

**Context and Nuance**
It is important to separate the verified facts from narrative embellishment. The $26.7 million was not a secretive contract for a "Bundibugyo-only" mRNA injection waiting in a freezer. It was a transparently announced research grant for multivalent filovirus vaccines, using two different technological platforms, aimed at a family of viruses that public health agencies have monitored for decades. Bundibugyo was named as one target among several--not the sole focus.

However, the coincidence remains legitimate fodder for scrutiny. The 2026 outbreak marks only the third known emergence of Bundibugyo virus in history, after 2007 and 2012. For CEPI to allocate specific multivalent funding explicitly naming this obscure strain, only for that exact strain to spark the first major international Ebola emergency in years within the same calendar quarter, is a notable alignment of preparedness and probability.
The Bundibugyo virus is a rare, deadly, often sexually transmitted and diagnostically elusive member of the Ebola family with a roughly 30-50% fatality rate and no approved vaccine. CEPI's $26.7 million grant to Oxford, Leipzig University, and Moderna--announced on January 7, 2026--was designed to create next-generation, broadly protective vaccines against the entire filovirus family, Bundibugyo included, using both viral vector and mRNA technology. Four months later, the world faced its first Bundibugyo outbreak in over a decade. Whether the preclinical program can accelerate into a deployable countermeasure or is[leaky](https://substack.com/redirect/831e488d-6900-43d4-9a51-f21400d4838f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)like the Marek's disease vaccine remains to be seen, but the timeline underscores both the value and the eerie timing of pandemic preparedness investments.

# [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131968407/622924437/-1343999874?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTE1MWU2NTYtY2E1Ni1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=aquO4Y1mqL6OrwqpmgCPBGoLoPV6PYiamJbMO6LR1ZU=)
Peter, With just 11 days until ballots are counted, a lot has been happening in this race. Outside money is flooding in. The attacks keep coming. And you’ve been with me every step of the way. So I want to take a step back from all of that — and remind you why I got into this race to begin with. **[If you already know you're with us, you can chip in $3 right now and I'll see you on the other side. If you've got a minute, I'd love to tell you my story.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131968409/622924439/701031031?refcode=em-5.23.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTE1MWU2NTYtY2E1Ni1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=aquO4Y1mqL6OrwqpmgCPBGoLoPV6PYiamJbMO6LR1ZU=)** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131968410/622924441/701031031?refcode=em-5.23.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTE1MWU2NTYtY2E1Ni1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=aquO4Y1mqL6OrwqpmgCPBGoLoPV6PYiamJbMO6LR1ZU=) _Back in the day at Palla Elementary School in Bakersfield (Go Bulldogs!)_ I grew up in Bakersfield, the son of Mexican immigrants. My dad opened an auto shop here in 2006. My mom was a homemaker. We didn't have much — I shared a bunk bed in the living room with my brothers. On weekends, I worked the swap meet and helped out at the shop. Nobody in my family had ever gone to college. I was the first. I watched my parents work themselves to the bone in a Valley that wasn’t built for people like us. I watched my older brother navigate life as a DACA recipient, always one policy change away from losing everything. I watched my younger brother put on a uniform to serve this country as a Marine. The Central Valley made me who I am. And for a long time, I thought the best way I could give back was to teach. So I became a professor at College of the Sequoias and a school board trustee -- making sure kids in this Valley had more doors open to them than I did. But something kept nagging at me. CA-22 has been represented by David Valadao for years. He looked Central Valley families in the eye and promised us he would never cut Medicaid — which is a lifeline for hundreds of thousands of people in our district. Then he voted for Trump's budget bill and did exactly that. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131968411/622924443/701031031?refcode=em-5.23.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTE1MWU2NTYtY2E1Ni1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=aquO4Y1mqL6OrwqpmgCPBGoLoPV6PYiamJbMO6LR1ZU=) I was at those rallies with the nurses, farmworkers, and families who couldn't believe their representative had sold them out. And I kept thinking: someone has to run against him. Someone who actually knows what it means to need Medicaid. Someone who grew up and built a life here. So I got in. Not because I wanted to be something, but because I wanted to _do something_ \-- for the families who can't afford to see a doctor, for the parents who can't afford rent, for the kids growing up in a Valley with dirty air and broken promises and no one in Washington fighting for them. **[With 10 days to go, corporate interests and the Israel lobby are doing everything they can to stop us. We need to raise $12,000 before midnight tonight to keep our message in front of voters. clean_body: | = Peter, With just 11 days until ballots are counted, a lot has been happening in this race. Outside money is flooding in. The attacks keep coming. And you’ve been with me every step of the way. So I want to take a step back from all of that — and remind you why I got into this race to begin with. = = Back in the day at Palla Elementary School in Bakersfield (Go Bulldogs!) I grew up in Bakersfield, the son of Mexican immigrants. My dad opened an auto shop here in 2006. My mom was a homemaker. We didn't have much — I shared a bunk bed in the living room with my brothers. On weekends, I worked the swap meet and helped out at the shop. Nobody in my family had ever gone to college. I was the first. I watched my parents work themselves to the bone in a Valley that wasn’t built for people like us. I watched my older brother navigate life as a DACA recipient, always one policy change away from losing everything. I watched my younger brother put on a uniform to serve this country as a Marine. The Central Valley made me who I am. And for a long time, I thought the best way I could give back was to teach. So I became a professor at College of the Sequoias and a school board trustee -- making sure kids in this Valley had more doors open to them than I did. But something kept nagging at me. CA-22 has been represented by David Valadao for years. He looked Central Valley families in the eye and promised us he would never cut Medicaid — which is a lifeline for hundreds of thousands of people in our district. Then he voted for Trump's budget bill and did exactly that. = I was at those rallies with the nurses, farmworkers, and families who couldn't believe their representative had sold them out. And I kept thinking: someone has to run against him. Someone who actually knows what it means to need Medicaid. Someone who grew up and built a life here. So I got in. Not because I wanted to be something, but because I wanted to do something \-- for the families who can't afford to see a doctor, for the parents who can't afford rent, for the kids growing up in a Valley with dirty air and broken promises and no one in Washington fighting for them. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = For the Central Valley, Randy | With deep ties to our community and a lifelong commitment to justice and equity, Randy is running for Congress in California’s 22nd District to bring bold, compassionate leadership to Washington. | | Peter,

When I was in middle school, my parents told us we were having another baby.

I remember sitting at the table thinking about how tight things already were. Not because I wasn’t happy, but because I could see how hard my parents were working just to keep us afloat.

So I told them not to worry about my birthday that year. I didn’t need anything — we should save everything we can for my new sister.

That’s what growing up in the Central Valley looked like for my family, and it’s not all that different from what a lot of families here are still going through. [](http://clicksp.frostforcongress.com/f/a/ArnK0MgzG8u8g4RRvhQMqw~~/AAPPABA~/IoL7hwzm35Fuzzs2mn07Fg_dInyXFuzfnsdXbDroMv94pEac1F3zdKMo5dFJZP35cAGyr2SvxmolBNlpAAGgzZNUVOTnJXgQ5M-LSALMDv9OIQtEO0aCrk5L1ZIWd_mOAf5ObINnWtHivfm0WxBdq__wNn3gOp1eGZ7K3yvho8hi0ix2nXOaeruhNkLyc1_h6dkISMamxdB-NDQ-Tnbhn2hKxGWFkCiXvJ3bazdp2GMp6UpHedHyG0O2AxS_-riA4teo_j478Vqo21BAOhIMBwKNAd0Obync8QmEMVd5JHB1OciGOtWswsM_PVR47Kqo8QkZKxMWVQDSSoYKkkaVSP0prZylrNaTzWAzieWg54ZiTHxCPGXQrj7OzrY9gz9l) Weekends weren’t for hanging out. I was working with my dad — first at the swap meet, then later at the auto shop — doing whatever we could to help cover the bills. After my middle school graduation, while my friends went out to celebrate, I went back to work.

Those experiences shape how you see things.

**It’s a big part of why I chose to stay in the Valley — to teach and mentor students as a College professor, and to be part of a community that I believe in.** I’ve spent years working with young people who are carrying those same responsibilities right now, trying to build something better for themselves and their families.

It’s also why I get so frustrated watching politicians like David Valadao side with corporations and special interests instead of the people I grew up with — families who work hard and still feel like they’re being left behind.

I’m running for Congress to win the deal our families deserve.

[**_I’m not taking corporate PAC money. This campaign depends on people who understand what’s at stake and want to fight for something better. give what they can — because what happens here matters.

here.

something meaningful — one conversation at a time.

whether we keep New Hampshire blue.

subject: The biggest loser
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
Is there a bigger loser than Donald Trump?
Politico recently reported that federal judges have ruled against Trump’s illegal ICE policies more than 10,000 times. That’s roughly 90 percent of all cases brought.
In each and every one of these cases, we’re talking about real people with real families:
Parents ripped away from their kids, picked up by ICE in the school drop-off line or while heading to church. Children as young as four years old traumatized and punished, appearing in court alone and facing deportation. People with lawful status arrested and detained at the courthouse before their immigration hearing.
Immigrants who've lived in this country for decades, disappeared into a detention system where phones don't work, lawyers can't get through, and no one knows where they are.
And by now, the Trump administration has made it clear these brutal tactics were never about upholding the law and protecting public safety. How could they be, if they’re actively breaking the law and making our communities less safe?
The cruelty has always been the point. Visible and commonplace enough that we become desensitized to the brutality and pain — enough that we stop speaking out.
But I won't, and I don't think you will either.
I will not stop fighting to end mass detention and shut down the horrific family detention centers that are profiting from human rights abuses.
Right now, federal judges are holding the line, but it’s up to us to push the work forward. We need to win elections. We need to take back the House and shut down the corrupt, chaotic, and cruel MAGA majority that’s enabling this brutal administration.
Will you join my efforts to flip the House with a contribution of any amount today? | | | Friend, A few weeks ago, I stood on a stage to receive the Catholic Champion Award. It was a humbling moment.

But as I held that award in my hands, I was not thinking about Hollywood. I was thinking about the children. And the millions of people who have joined this fight to protect them. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am a producer, actor, and founder of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**.

Families were being destroyed.

And most people had no idea this evil even existed.

That is why I helped produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame. **
**Not for awards. **But because I believed people needed to see the truth. For years, many in Hollywood said the movie would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But we refused.** Because when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.

Will you join the fight? | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, A few weeks ago, I stood on a stage to receive the Catholic Champion Award. It was a humbling moment. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am a producer, actor, and founder of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Years ago, after hearing firsthand stories about children trapped in trafficking, my life changed forever. What I learned broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold for profit. Families were being destroyed. And most people had no idea this evil even existed. That is why I helped produce the film Sound of Freedom. Not for fame. Not for awards. But because I believed people needed to see the truth. For years, many in Hollywood said the movie would never succeed. Doors closed. Studios walked away. People told us to give up. But we refused. Because when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option. Today, the Sound of Freedom Foundation continues that mission beyond the movie screen. We exist to stop the sale of God 's children and protect vulnerable children from exploitation and trafficking. This work is real. Every day, traffickers target children who are vulnerable, isolated, poor, or forgotten. And every day, we fight back through prevention, rescue support, education, awareness, and advocacy. We help strengthen struggling families before traffickers can prey on them. We equip trusted rescue partners working to save children trapped in exploitation. We educate parents and communities about the warning signs traffickers use to target children. And we push leaders to take stronger action against those who profit from abuse. Jesus said, " Let the little children come to me... for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these." (Matthew 19:14)I believe every child is created by God with dignity, value, and purpose. And I believe we are called to protect them and that's**why I am reaching out to you today. Will you make your first gift to help defend vulnerable children and stop trafficking? When I accepted the Catholic Champion Award, I said: "I made a promise to God, to dedicate my life to ending child trafficking because God 's children are not for sale." That promise still guides everything we do. But this mission is bigger than one person. It takes people willing to stand up and say, " No more." Please join us today. Together, we can shine light into darkness. We can protect innocent children and help bring freedom to those who need it most. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

There are only ten days left before an incredible climate champion faces his primary election in my home state of California. clean_body: Hi, it’s Eileen Laubacher, the Democrat and retired U.S. Navy Admiral running against Lauren Boebert here in Colorado. Hello, My name is Eileen Laubacher, and I am the Democrat and retired U.S. Navy Rear Admiral running against Lauren Boebert here in Colorado. I was 17-years-old the first time I raised my right hand and took an oath to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic. I took those words, and that responsibility, seriously every day for the next 4 decades. When I was an intelligence officer. When I was deployed to Afghanistan. When I became an Admiral. And as a member of the president’s National Security Council. But in all those years, I have never felt as much of a threat to our country, our Constitution, and our very democracy as I do right now. I said I would never run for office. But in this moment, I feel an obligation to step up, serve my community, and defend our country once again. I am running for Congress to defeat Lauren Boebert because when she was sworn into office, Lauren took a similar oath to defend our Constitution – and she has betrayed it almost every single day since then. Adam Frisch only lost to Lauren Boebert by 546 votes. It was the closest race in the entire country. We can finally put an end to Lauren Boebert’s embarrassing political career – but I need your help now to do it. Our campaign needs to raise another $100,000 before our deadline at midnight to defeat Lauren Boebert and take back the House for Democrats, but right now, we’re still short. If I am going to send Lauren Boebert packing and flip this seat blue, I need grassroots donors like you to chip in right now to my campaign: = Please use the links in this email to start a monthly donation through ActBlue: | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Our republic is being tested in ways that it has never been before. And what if you knew that all across the country, Democratic women up and down the ballot are counting on the EMILYs List community to help propel them to victory in the general election? Are you ready to support their campaigns with a $15 donation today? We know that $15 may not seem like enough to make such a big impact. But Peter, it’s not just you making a $15 contribution. By the time you’ve gotten to this point in this message, people from all across the country who support our movement to elect Democratic pro-choice candidates have read this email and already made their own $15 donations. Now, they’re hoping you’ll do the same. Taking back power this November is a team effort, and we need you in this fight. = | = = Thanks for hearing us out. We’re so grateful you’re on our team. \- EMILYs List | = | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you for being a supporter of EMILYs List. This email was sent to: dpwillis67@gmail.com. Inbox overcrowded? May 23, 2026
Connecticut's Democrats are spoiled. No matter whom they nominate, that person wins. It's a Deep Blue state. When you add up the number of municipal and state workers (retired or not), those on public assistance, freeloaders and Trump-hating affluent white liberals who have nothing else to do but attend No Kings rallies, the number exceeds 50%.
But it is possible for a Republican to win. But the Democratic vote needs to split. This happened in 1994 when Republican John Rowland won with 36% while more liberal voters split, with Democrat Bill Curry receiving 33% and independent Eunice Groark receiving 19%.
Could this happen in 2026? Definitely. And it is up to a party called [The Working Families Party (WFP).](https://substack.com/redirect/1bd2c851-071c-4173-a072-1bf6e89f36fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

State Representative, [Josh Elliott](https://substack.com/redirect/235fba6e-ce22-423c-a984-d4820192aa76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Hamden, has emerged from the Left to challenge Governor Lamont. A self-described "leading progressive voice," Representative Elliott is an [unabashed liberal](https://substack.com/redirect/1c96ceec-42f3-428b-8dcc-5abfb17a9bfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who supports increasing taxes on the wealthy, government sponsored childcare, universal health care, rent control, forced low-income housing in Connecticut's affluent towns, using taxpayer money to pay striking workers (I do not have enough imagination to make this up), ranked-choice voting and believes the best way to combat criminal thuggery is rehabilitation and counselling (I am not making this up either).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4800ff00-c728-4047-8a12-75ed9f7148cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Representative Josh Elliott

He even believes that allowing more roof top solar panels and banning natural gas in Connecticut will reduce energy costs!

He probably thinks Bernie Saunders is a right-wing nut job.

But Governor Lamont has morphed into a Fairfield County Republican and liberals are livid. Lamont has refused to raise taxes on the wealthy because he fears they could leave the state. He vetoed an aggressive attempt by liberal Democrats to change local zoning laws in municipalities to increase affordable housing. And he does not believe striking workers should be subsidized by taxpayers.

But in spite Connecticut's reputation for progressive policies, it has a feudal remnant to prevent gadflies from challenging the statue quo, the Convention System. In almost every state, if you want to run for public office, you need to garner a certain number of signatures to be placed on the ballot.

But not in Connecticut. Each party has a Town Committee in every town. Members from these committees meet at a convention and choose their candidates. But to place your name on the primary ballot, you need to garner 15% of the delegates. And this is very difficult to do when your opponent is party insider and especially if your opponent is a sitting Governor.

This is why I went into fits of uncontrollable laughter when I read Representative Elliott was attempting to receive 15% at the Democratic convention. I have personally sought nominations as a Republican for both US Senate and Congress and participated in running the conventions for my good friend Mike Goldstein as he ran for Congress in Fairfield County. Many of these convention delegates are party hacks angling for state and local jobs. And Josh Elliott was going to get 15% against a sitting Democratic Governor who controls many of these jobs? What a joke. The guy was out of his mind.

And boy was I wrong. Elliott received 25% and, by his own admission, would have won the Convention if there had been secret ballots. The media were too dense to report what a remarkable accomplishment this was. And it means Elliott has a huge amount of support and could become Governor if he is the nominee.

Elliott will now face Lamont in a primary in August, and he has qualified to receive $3.7 million from the state. His problem is that $3.7 million is a rounding error to the billionaire Lamont (strange how the media never point this out) who could blow $20 million to stop Elliott.
But the persistent Elliott has an ace up his sleeve. There is a third party in Connecticut that has access to a ballot line in the November general election, the [Working Families Party (WFP)](https://substack.com/redirect/1bd2c851-071c-4173-a072-1bf6e89f36fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It consists of only 300 members and to say these people are left of center would be a gross understatement.
The WFP could choose an unknown. But this carries a risk. According to Connecticut election law, a political party must receive at least 1% of the vote in the previous election to have a line in the next election. If an unknown WFP candidate fails to do this, the WFP risks political oblivion.

The WFP could also be total wimps, hold their nose and nominate Lamont. Why? Because this makes a Lamont victory quite likely. The Republican moderate Erin Stewart may have given Lamont a tough race heads up, but a scandal on her use of her expense account while she was mayor of New Britian ended her campaign. The more conservative Republican nominee Ryan Fazio has a chance, but the betting sites such as Polymarket put it at 7%.

But if the WFP honors its values and nominates Elliott, then all hell breaks loose. According to the Connecticut State Election Commission, Elliott cannot receive state funding if he switches parties. But he can raise money on his own and the August primary will make his name recognition and position on the issues well known to Connecticut liberals. He could easily win 20% and put Fazio in the Governor's mansion or pull 35% and win! But if Fazio wins, the WFP will surely be blamed. And they know this.

Governor Lamont has ties to the WFP and has been nominated by them before. One of his high-level advisors, [Matthew Brokman](https://substack.com/redirect/a4b3ad51-2672-46de-af82-04ae1fc34766?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is married former WFP chairman Lindsey Farrell. Lamont will surely do everything in his power to secure the WFP nomination.

What does this mean?

It means I am pretending to be a liberal so I can join the WFP. I want to be invited to Governor's Lamont's barbecues at his Greenwich estate. And just to let Governor Lamont know, I prefer Old Rip Van Winkle Bourbon in my Manhattans, the 2009 Chateau Lafite Rothschild (please make sure to decant it properly) and my filet mignons rare.

Each party has a Town Committee in every town. Members from these committees meet at a convention and choose their candidates. But to place your name on the primary ballot, you need to garner 15% of the delegates. And this is very difficult to do when your opponent is party insider and especially if your opponent is a sitting Governor. This is why I went into fits of uncontrollable laughter when I read Representative Elliott was attempting to receive 15% at the Democratic convention. I have personally sought nominations as a Republican for both US Senate and Congress and participated in running the conventions for my good friend Mike Goldstein as he ran for Congress in Fairfield County. Many of these convention delegates are party hacks angling for state and local jobs. And Josh Elliott was going to get 15% against a sitting Democratic Governor who controls many of these jobs? What a joke. The guy was out of his mind. And boy was I wrong. Elliott received 25% and, by his own admission, would have won the Convention if there had been secret ballots. The media were too dense to report what a remarkable accomplishment this was. And it means Elliott has a huge amount of support and could become Governor if he is the nominee. Elliott will now face Lamont in a primary in August, and he has qualified to receive $3.7 million from the state. His problem is that $3.7 million is a rounding error to the billionaire Lamont (strange how the media never point this out) who could blow $20 million to stop Elliott. But the persistent Elliott has an ace up his sleeve. There is a third party in Connecticut that has access to a ballot line in the November general election, the . It consists of only 300 members and to say these people are left of center would be a gross understatement. The WFP could choose an unknown. But this carries a risk. According to Connecticut election law, a political party must receive at least 1% of the vote in the previous election to have a line in the next election. If an unknown WFP candidate fails to do this, the WFP risks political oblivion. The WFP could also be total wimps, hold their nose and nominate Lamont. Why? Because this makes a Lamont victory quite likely. The Republican moderate Erin Stewart may have given Lamont a tough race heads up, but a scandal on her use of her expense account while she was mayor of New Britian ended her campaign. The more conservative Republican nominee Ryan Fazio has a chance, but the betting sites such as Polymarket put it at 7%. But if the WFP honors its values and nominates Elliott, then all hell breaks loose. According to the Connecticut State Election Commission, Elliott cannot receive state funding if he switches parties. But he can raise money on his own and the August primary will make his name recognition and position on the issues well known to Connecticut liberals. He could easily win 20% and put Fazio in the Governor's mansion or pull 35% and win! But if Fazio wins, the WFP will surely be blamed. And they know this. Governor Lamont has ties to the WFP and has been nominated by them before. One of his high-level advisors, , is married former WFP chairman Lindsey Farrell. Lamont will surely do everything in his power to secure the WFP nomination. What does this mean? It means I am pretending to be a liberal so I can join the WFP. I want to be invited to Governor's Lamont's barbecues at his Greenwich estate. And just to let Governor Lamont know, I prefer Old Rip Van Winkle Bourbon in my Manhattans, the 2009 Chateau Lafite Rothschild (please make sure to decant it properly) and my filet mignons rare. Peter,

People are angry about the redrawn maps. They should be. clean_body: I am going to keep on pushing on. | | | | | Peter, While the Tennessee General Assembly was at the Capitol carving up congressional districts, I was in living rooms across Middle Tennessee talking to real people about real issues. People are angry about the redrawn maps. They should be. But when you sit down with someone at their kitchen table, the conversation always comes back to the same things: grocery bills that keep climbing, healthcare they can't afford, childcare they can't find, gas prices that make every errand feel like a decision. Those are the conversations that remind me exactly why I'm running. And those are the conversations that no amount of gerrymandering can stop us from having. The politicians can draw whatever lines they want. They cannot draw a line between the people of this district and me. We are going to keep showing up, keep knocking doors, keep sitting at kitchen tables, and keep building this campaign one conversation at a time. Peter,

It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**

clean_body: Join me| | | Peter, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Peter, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Peter, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. | | | | | WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250**th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Peter, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Sincerely, Gary Sinise Honarary Grand MarshalNational Memorial Day Parade P.S. Peter, America is stepping into its 250th year, and this Memorial Day begins that national remembrance. Veterans across generations have given their lives to defend America and all she stands for. And for the Greatest Generation in particular, this may be the last time they're able to join us at this year's National Memorial Day Parade. There's no better send-off we can give them than to make sure they're present to honor their fallen brethren during America's 250th birthday. For years, the Left thought they had a permanent grip on America's youth.

| | | | [](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=a341cf4d34d144acbaa8388ba67ba358&_e=VJgtlawUPMvu5WSH2gf4HszIBhklthb89L5lX_lkILt7t_akA_9cngtyjiLZRWe1mzio8UbWqiK9rbgX2LHkkOK5BhwBIXxWD3d4R7i_pA2CVMINp-zs7d-hmbX_st398hW9jDEUN3I-daKygXzPY3g2X9SyvuJN0db6835Jh9Uza61DfgqM4UvcasBXcgNMaCgOa_nfDYPIOYcqH8QDBDrG19utEr7GSpcs3lKAgDavluo1SUCxNn2aHqJW3I79krMyanQ8q-Vcz5bMhxWE8Yhva8URgzP_b_OMGzOrtW20S_oL59uGI1t80DMQh18ZSDiwEUh8zqr9EQtnJJyWSMh5tMo8E51PTZFXMO4zuA7Z0aHDRXG7f8_H6RDIPFcNNtRKyUEz-tDBsjol7h1b6YbC9fe6i6y4HJj9DV7wOYv9MCyn85jl2Z_64NC4qAjpOgkL97Zv7DGwd5prLg2oy9AGTlK3xiKQG1h6ChA0-VK8AJAEXGYAptBVUd3uyKoGTj5jLCf3uKVK3N3ESupXoGrEqmhmS9TVuYu5oyWHQokKYQqJ9rJZQ7xWncptVuYKsWqnzjlS86q1PtpmDvhNhMASup1CZFYqDuLiB3itCdpXemb0fS1cSM-ynx4aWoJIi_1PQMKW1GdI7EfrR7XfGJHx6oQzZbUN-qXEXzoiRptPVDevqEsNCjbhgah-_yVo)
